::: {.block title="Introduction"}
Resolving the spatiotemporal variability of chlorophyll *a* (Chl *a*) throughout the euphotic zone, including subsurface chlorophyll maxima, helps characterize phytoplankton distributions and constrain estimates of depth-integrated primary production. Previous research (Sauzède et al., 2016, 2025) has established that satellite remote-sensing reflectance (R~rs~) at multiple bands can be used to infer subsurface Chl *a* concentration and locations of subsurface chlorophyll peaks in the open ocean. In this study, we use a similar model ("CHLA-Z") to explore whether hyperspectral information (172 R~rs~ bands from NASA's Plankton, Aerosol, Cloud, ocean Ecosystem (PACE) mission) improves subsurface Chl *a* estimation and whether the approach transfers to coastal waters.

Predictions are from models that saw no data from the profile's 1° cell within its 30-day block.](figures/fig_example_profiles.png){#fig-examples script="scripts/fig_example_profiles.py" width="100%"}

```{=typst}
#v(0.15in)
```

**Relation to existing approaches.** The Copernicus Marine 3D chlorophyll product (SOCA2024; Sauzède et al., 2025) predicts weekly 0.25° Chl *a* profiles for water deeper than 1000 m, using neural networks trained on BGC-Argo with 5-band R~rs~ plus physical fields; it currently ends in December 2023. Our aim is not to replace it but to study what R~rs~ alone can tell us about subsurface Chl *a*. CHLA-Z uses daily hyperspectral PACE R~rs~ without physics, adds Ocean Observatories Initiative (OOI) moorings and gliders to BGC-Argo for the slope and shelf, and uses boosted regression trees.

```{=typst}
#v(0.3in)
#text(size: 0.75em)[*Reference.* Sauzède, R., Renosh, P.R., Schmechtig, C., Uitz, J., and Claustre, H. (2025). Quality Information Document, MULTIOBS\_GLO\_BIO\_BGC\_3D\_REP\_015\_010, issue 5.0. Copernicus Marine Service.]
```

:::
